record.paper_title: From P systems to morphogenetic systems: an overview and open problems
record.context_brief: Virus spread in M-system cell populations
record.original_question: Model viruses as geometrically simple agents inside a population of cells represented by a morphogenetic system, and use the model to simulate and analyze how viral infection spreads through that cell population. Develop the model so that its predictions are meaningful at the level of macro-observables rather than only at the level of microscopic simulation details.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 6 Viruses are objects with a simple geometry and behavior. Simulate and study spreading of viruses in a cell population, try to make the model relevant at the level of macro-observables.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A morphogenetic system (M-system) is a discrete spatial computational model in which a population of agents — called cells — is represented by collections of geometrically embedded tiles (e.g., polygons or polyhedra) that interact through local rules governing self-assembly, division, signaling, and degradation. Each cell occupies a bounded region of Euclidean space, has a membrane composed of tiles, and evolves under stochastic local interaction rules that may produce, consume, or transform tiles based on geometric contact and local concentrations of signal objects.

Within this framework, model viruses as additional agents of simple geometry and behavior (for example, small rigid tiles or compact tile assemblies) that diffuse in the spatial environment, attach to compatible cell membrane tiles, enter cells, replicate inside them by consuming intracellular resources to produce copies of themselves, and are released upon cell lysis or by budding through the membrane.

Tasks:
1. Formally define such a virus-augmented M-system, specifying the tile types representing virions, the rules for virion–cell attachment, entry, intracellular replication, and release, and the spatial diffusion mechanism for free virions.
2. Use this model to simulate the spread of viral infection through a population of cells.
3. Establish that the model yields predictions that are meaningful at the level of macro-observables — for instance, the time evolution of the number of infected cells, the basic reproduction number, total viral load, or spatial infection front speed — and not merely at the level of microscopic simulation traces. In particular, derive or empirically validate relationships between the local M-system parameters (rates of attachment, entry, replication, lysis, diffusion) and macroscopic epidemiological quantities, comparing them where possible to classical compartmental (e.g., SIR-type) descriptions of viral spread in tissue.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not find any published work that explicitly models virus spread within morphogenetic (M-)systems and validates predictions at the level of macro-observables. The problem appears as an open challenge in the morphogenetic systems literature, and no resolution was located.

status_evidence.title: Morphogenetic systems overview (zbMATH 7395482)
status_evidence.snippet: Listed open problems for morphogenetic systems include simulating viral spread in cell populations with models meaningful at macro-observable level.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem in the morphogenetic systems framework with no published resolution found.
